artists.name: Augustė Vickunaitė & Zara Joan Miller (duo)
artists.bio:
AUGUSTĖ VICKUNAITĖ has worked with reel-to-reel tape recorders since 2016 — playing them, recording to them, and letting the decay of the machines take part.

Found material, field recordings, voice, objects and the whole spectrum of the equipment's malfunctions are layered against each other: tape music and collage, theatrical, darkly funny, in no hurry. She has played Cafe OTO, KM28, the Volksbühne, Seanaps and Braille Satellite.

artists.name: Deeat Palace
artists.bio:
Brussels. Electronic and improvised music built largely on a Serge modular system — the first record, Pièces pour Serge, is two long pieces for that instrument alone.

Since then: s.canners on Prix Libre, releases on MIND Records and Erratum Musical, and a live practice that runs from trance-inducing repetition to something closer to folk.

artists.name: bivou4c
artists.bio:
A DJ from Paris, in Brussels — after strength in shared bass amplitudes, as they put it themselves.

Half of the label Bientôt Veuves, and a regular at Métaphore collectif nights between Paris and Marseille.

artists.name: Marc Matter
artists.bio:
Born in Basel in 1974, working in Düsseldorf. A founding member of Institut fuer Feinmotorik and, on his own, a maker of serial word compositions and sample-poetry — speech fragments lifted from news headlines and advertising, layered and repeated until they become material.

He studied at the Kunsthochschule für Medien in Cologne, has taught music and text at the IMM in Düsseldorf since 2010, and won the Karl Sczuka Prize for radio art in 2011 for Die 50 Skulpturen des Institut fuer Feinmotorik.

artists.name: Tresque
artists.bio:
TRESQUE is Laurent Peter, who also performs as d'incise and runs the INSUB. label — the name is taken from a half-forgotten medieval dance and put to work as an idea of techno.

The music is carved in circular movements out of samples and amplified noise, dub technique on one side and musique concrète on the other, grooves reduced to their shortest form and held between standing still and moving.

artists.name: Zohastre
artists.bio:
French-italian duo, whirlwind combination of spacio-tribal drums and bewitched electronics. Conjuring up harrowing medieval spirits & tripped out bag-pipe merriment with complex and repetitive rhythmic patterns, ethereal undulating sounds and guttural sub bass.

Like troubadours from outer space, ZOHASTRE venture into an hallucinated quest, ecstatic and psychedelic cavalcade, through the night, the forest, the universe. Practicing hypnotic audio gestures, they unleash impro-ritualistic music for trance-like FX.

artists.name: Gaute Granli
artists.bio:
GAUTE GRANLI works alone in Stavanger: voice, guitar, a bank of effects and an analogue sampler, run through each other until the parts stop being separable. Chanting over feedback, rhythm arrived at by accident, a one-man band that sounds like a bad transmission of a larger one.

He played guitar and shouted in Skadne Krek and Freddy The Dyke before the solo work took over. Records have come out on Drid Machine, Ultra Eczema, Editions Cave12, Nashazphone and Feeding Tube — the most recent, Bløt Klut, in 2024.

artists.name: Lucie Páchová & Maryia Kamarova
artists.bio:
❦ live for voiced objects and objected voices.

LUCIE PÁCHOVÁ’s practice across sound, voice and composition approaches sound as a relational and physical experience. Her work is rooted in listening to landscapes, voices, animals, everyday environments and the materiality of objects. It spans sound collages, multichannel sound installations, audiovisual works, solo performances, interdisciplinary collaborations, and compositions for chamber ensembles and orchestras. She is based in Prague.

MARYIA KAMAROVA's practice is situated at the intersection of sound art, performance, and installation.
She creates spatial settings and in-situ interventions that employ displaced and reassembled objects, embracing material agency and human failure. In her recent work, she explores how sound artifacts emerge across different levels of amplification, while playing with their acoustic presence and its sonified reflection. Maryia presented her work internationally and overseas.

artists.name: Giulia Rae
artists.bio:
GIULIA RAE is a sound artist based in Brussels. Active in the Italian experimental music scene since 2016, she later expanded her path internationally, performing and releasing her music on labels such as Mappa, Søvn Records, Riforma, while composing acousmatic music for multiple formats.

She sometimes appears as a radio selector and works as a composer and sound designer for film, dance, performance, and multidisciplinary projects. Grounded in creative coding, Giulia Rae’s livesets form wide sonic spaces made of synthetic textures, concrete sounds, processed voice and enveloping bass.

artists.name: Eve Julia Gonzalez & Myles Dillon
artists.bio:
EVE: Hungry for sad melodies and minor figures, I have no interest in hierarchy or positivity.
Through rhizomatic installations that mainly combine drawing, text and objects, I try to capture the moment a crisis takes shape. Through an aesthetic of lament and melancholic childhood, I address a crisis born of the clamour of existence, set somewhat against the world. Yet I compose in collaboration with the world, and it is within its carcass that my practice peels away from illustration to become an extension of drawing into space.
It is a cryptic trail through which I try to explore some of the meanders of identity, of the world and of our relation to others. I have also developed a performance and video practice, and this side of my work borders on spectacle: a spectacle that makes no secret of its artificiality. Performance acts as a binder that brings together gesture, people, words and music. I try to give material form to the pain that life can bring.

MYLES: My musical language draws on heterogeneous aesthetics, from Baroque music to modern and contemporary composition, and from electroacoustic music to the electronic music of British rave culture, especially ambient, jungle and acid. These influences meet in a written, fixed-media music, where memory, abstraction and spectromorphological and polyphonic writing open listening spaces to perceptions and imaginaries in perpetual collapse.
Each composition grows out of a process of collecting, listening and sound generation. Analog and modular synthesis, electronic instrument-making, experimental recording and personal or historical archives form bodies of material in which sounds become traces of intimate and collective memory.

artists.name: UBLO
artists.bio:
To celebrate the release of UBLO's tape “Split Replica” on Third Type Tapes in November '26, the label organizes a mini-tour with stops in Paris, Nancy and Brussels (9-10-11th Nov).
UBLO is the electronic solo of Gabriel Valtchev. He detaches himself from aesthetic restrictions to immerse himself in the accidental, the sensory and confusion, whether physical or emotional.
He is also drumming in bands R999D, Otto and Vava Maudit.

artists.name: LIME68K
artists.bio:
Prolific and playing with blurred boundaries, LIME68K creates improvised music on stage that is at once demanding, 
danceable, and breathtaking, using live coding and various instruments and tools she has developed. 
Her soundscape never stops and is constantly evolving. 
Recognized by the legendary British electronic duo Autechre, for whom she opened in Rennes in 2024, 
she has released various projects on fals.ch, Active Listeners Club, EVEL, and Miniature Recs...

artists.name: FATIGUE SUSPECTE
artists.bio:
FATIGUE SUSPECTE is a noise techno sound and music experimentation project founded in 2018 by Luc Le Manchot and Suliane Hamon. 
Their music is largely based on sampling and field recording. 
They explore various techniques for deconstructing samples, such as granular synthesis and extreme bitcrushing.
The rhythmic aspect is characterized by a blend of analog and digital sounds. 
The resulting sound allows for the development of patterns in which the improvisation of sequences leads to a strange, lopsided groove. 
The composition of Fatigue Suspecte’s tracks and live performances blends cinematic storytelling with techno progression. 
The atmosphere created draws heavily on horror films as well as elements from folklore.
The harmonic aspect draws on traditional music, while the rhythms deviate from the four-beat structure of techno through the layering of polyrhythms and irregular rhythms.

artists.name: & COMPAGNIE
artists.bio:
& COMPAGNIE is the solo project by one half of 2Mo.
The music of "& Compagnie" is crafted using homemade tools built with SuperCollider.
Situated somewhere between live coding and non-visual performance, "& Compagnie" delivers its twisted interpretation of rather abrupt music that lies somewhere between distorted breakcore and repetitive, hypnotic, ever-evolving rhythms.
4649 ("YOROSHIKU") is the electronic duo of Csocsó and Doresale, where textual improvisation and the disarticulation of textures and rhythms form quasi-songs that celebrate their build-up failures.

artists.name: Bobé Van Jézu
artists.bio:
BOBÉ VAN JÉZU is part of the THIRDTYPETAPES label and host of the monthly TTTINTAMARE radio show.
His mixes ground in illbient and deconstructed rhythmic oddities, hazes of floating presences and ghost-like patterns.

artists.name: REFUS D'OBTEMPÉRER
artists.bio:
REFUS D'OBTEMPÉRER is a live project that seeks to play with the conventions of dancehall, 
rap, and noise to manipulate vocal samples and make small, modified electronic machines scream. 
Beyond the deep bass, swaying snare drums, and distorted kicks, 
the project is about championing the accessibility and diversity of urban and underground countercultures through an anti-establishment attitude.
